Bank of America confirmed the loss of its employee in an emailed statement to Reuters: “We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said.
According to officials, a woman carrying multiple knives stabbed two people in Times Square before police intervened.

Bank of America shares showed little reaction to the news, with markets treating the incident as an isolated personnel tragedy rather than a corporate event.

The bank employs tens of thousands of staff across its global corporate and investment banking division, where Piacenti’s role in business selection and conflicts sits within compliance-adjacent functions that vet deals before they move forward.
